title: Face relation and poset structure on the induced space G ×^P X'
body_html:
Face relation and poset structure on the induced space

Fix the induction data $(G', P)$ satisfying (P0)–(P2) and the induced space $X = G \times^P X'$ of [[node:equivariant_sheaves.induction_GxP_X]], with $\iota : X' \hookrightarrow X$, $E \mapsto [(1, E)]$.

The face relation on $X$ has to be introduced by hand — $X$ is only a set-theoretic quotient — and then shown to make $X$ a partial order.

Definition

Definition (face relation on $X$). For $x, y \in X$, $$ x \;\preceq\; y \iff \exists\, g \in G,\; \exists\, F \preceq E \text{ in } X',\quad x = [(g, F)] \text{ and } y = [(g, E)]. $$

In prose: $x \preceq y$ means $x$ and $y$ admit representatives $(g, F)$ and $(g, E)$ with the same first coordinate $g$ such that $F \preceq E$ in $X'$. Both sides of the definition are existentially quantified over the representative choice, so the definition is manifestly independent of representatives — no separate well-definedness proposition needed for the "definition level" content.

This is exactly the generator obtained by pushing the face relation of $X'$ into $X$ via a common $G$-orbit: $$ g \cdot \iota F \;\preceq\; g \cdot \iota E \qquad (F \preceq E \text{ in } X'). $$ The class of pairs meeting the definition is precisely the image of this generator on the quotient.

No reflexive-transitive closure is needed. The ambient equivalence relation $\sim$ (which lets us shift representatives) absorbs all closure steps into a single generator on classes; that this "single-step generator" is already transitive on classes is proved as Theorem 2 below (using (P0), (P1)).

Reflexivity is built in. For any class $y = [(g, E)]$, take $F := E$; then $F \preceq E$ in $X'$ (reflexivity of the base poset), and $x := y = [(g, E)] = [(g, F)]$ witnesses $y \preceq y$.

Equivalent characterisation

Theorem 1 (single-witness form). For $(g_1, E_1), (g_2, E_2) \in G \times X'$, $$ [(g_1, E_1)] \;\preceq\; [(g_2, E_2)] \;\iff\; \exists\, n \in G',\quad n \cdot E_1 \preceq E_2 \text{ in } X' \;\wedge\; g_1^{-1} g_2 n \in P_{E_1}. $$

Compare with the equivalence relation $\sim$ of [[node:equivariant_sheaves.induction_GxP_X]]: replacing $\preceq$ on $X'$ by $=$ recovers $\sim$ verbatim. The face relation and the equivalence relation share the same syntactic shape.
proof_html:
($\Rightarrow$) Assume the definition: there exist $g \in G$ and $F \preceq E$ in $X'$ with $[(g_1, E_1)] = [(g, F)]$ and $[(g_2, E_2)] = [(g, E)]$. Unpacking the two $\sim$-equalities: $\exists n_1 \in G'$, $n_1 E_1 = F$, $g_1^{-1} g n_1 \in P_{E_1}$; and $\exists n_2 \in G'$, $n_2 E_2 = E$, $g_2^{-1} g n_2 \in P_{E_2}$. Combining $F = n_1 E_1$ with $F \preceq E = n_2 E_2$ gives $n_1 E_1 \preceq n_2 E_2$, i.e.\ $n_2^{-1} n_1 E_1 \preceq E_2$.

Take $n := n_2^{-1} n_1 \in G'$. The face-chain condition is done. For the residual $g_1^{-1} g_2 n \in P_{E_1}$: substituting $g = g_1 p_1 n_1^{-1}$ (from the first $\sim$, with $p_1 := g_1^{-1} g n_1 \in P_{E_1}$) and $g = g_2 p_2 n_2^{-1}$ (from the second, with $p_2 := g_2^{-1} g n_2 \in P_{E_2}$) gives $g_1 p_1 n_1^{-1} = g_2 p_2 n_2^{-1}$, so $g_1^{-1} g_2 = p_1 n_1^{-1} n_2 p_2^{-1}$, and $$ g_1^{-1} g_2 n = p_1 n_1^{-1} n_2 p_2^{-1} n_2^{-1} n_1 = p_1 \cdot n_1^{-1} (n_2 p_2^{-1} n_2^{-1}) n_1. $$ Now $n_2 p_2^{-1} n_2^{-1} \in n_2 P_{E_2} n_2^{-1} = P_{n_2 E_2} = P_E$ by (P1), and $F \preceq E$ gives $P_E \le P_F = P_{n_1 E_1}$ by (P0); finally $n_1^{-1} P_{n_1 E_1} n_1 = P_{E_1}$ by (P1). So the second factor lies in $P_{E_1}$; combined with $p_1 \in P_{E_1}$, the product is in $P_{E_1}$.

($\Leftarrow$) Assume the single-witness form with witness $n \in G'$. Take $g := g_2$, $F := n E_1$, $E := E_2$. Then $F \preceq E$ (given). We must check $[(g_1, E_1)] = [(g_2, F)] = [(g_2, n E_1)]$ and $[(g_2, E_2)] = [(g_2, E_2)]$.

The second is trivial. For the first, apply $\sim$ with witness $m := n$: $m E_1 = n E_1 = F$, and $g_1^{-1} g_2 n \in P_{E_1}$ (given). So the definition holds with these choices. $\square$

The single-witness form is the pre-quotient relation $\preceq_{\text{rep}}$ on $G \times X'$: $$ (g_1, E_1) \preceq_{\text{rep}} (g_2, E_2) \;:\iff\; \exists\, n \in G',\;\; n \cdot E_1 \preceq E_2 \;\text{and}\; g_1^{-1} g_2 n \in P_{E_1}. $$ It is the form used in every downstream calculation.

Transitivity

Theorem 2 (transitivity). Under (P0) and (P1), $\preceq$ on $X$ is transitive.

Equivalently, $\preceq_{\text{rep}}$ on $G \times X'$ is transitive.

Proof. Given witnesses $n_1$ for $(g_1, E_1) \preceq_{\text{rep}} (g_2, E_2)$ and $n_2$ for $(g_2, E_2) \preceq_{\text{rep}} (g_3, E_3)$, take $n := n_2 n_1 \in G'$.

Face-chain. $n \cdot E_1 = n_2 \cdot (n_1 \cdot E_1) \preceq n_2 \cdot E_2 \preceq E_3$, using cellularity of $n_2$ (preserves $\preceq$) and transitivity of $\preceq$ on $X'$.

Residual. Set $p_1 := g_1^{-1} g_2 n_1 \in P_{E_1}$ and $p_2 := g_2^{-1} g_3 n_2 \in P_{E_2}$. Then $$ g_1^{-1} g_3 (n_2 n_1) = (g_1^{-1} g_2)(g_2^{-1} g_3 n_2)(n_1) = (p_1 n_1^{-1}) p_2 n_1 = p_1 \cdot \bigl(n_1^{-1} p_2 n_1\bigr). $$

To conclude $g_1^{-1} g_3 n \in P_{E_1}$, we show $n_1^{-1} p_2 n_1 \in P_{E_1}$:

  • $p_2 \in P_{E_2}$.
  • From $n_1 \cdot E_1 \preceq E_2$ and (P0): $P_{E_2} \le P_{n_1 \cdot E_1}$, so $p_2 \in P_{n_1 \cdot E_1}$.
  • From (P1): $P_{n_1 \cdot E_1} = n_1 P_{E_1} n_1^{-1}$, i.e.\ $n_1^{-1} P_{n_1 \cdot E_1} n_1 = P_{E_1}$. Applying to $p_2$: $n_1^{-1} p_2 n_1 \in P_{E_1}$.

Hence $g_1^{-1} g_3 n = p_1 \cdot (n_1^{-1} p_2 n_1) \in P_{E_1} \cdot P_{E_1} = P_{E_1}$. $\square$

Where each axiom enters. (P0) lifts $p_2$ from $P_{E_2}$ into the larger $P_{n_1 \cdot E_1}$ along the face relation $n_1 E_1 \preceq E_2$. (P1) conjugates $P_{n_1 \cdot E_1}$ back to $P_{E_1}$ via $n_1 \in G'$. Neither can be dispensed with — a $P$ without cosheaf monotonicity or without $G'$-equivariance already breaks transitivity of the induced face relation.

Well-definedness on classes (descent of $\preceq_{\text{rep}}$)

The definition above uses a representative $(g, E)$ of the right-hand class; we now verify that the resulting relation on classes is independent of this choice. Equivalently: $\preceq_{\text{rep}}$ on $G \times X'$ is $\sim$-invariant on both arguments.

Proposition (descent). Under (P0) and (P1), for $(g_1, E_1) \sim (g_1', E_1')$ and $(g_2, E_2) \sim (g_2', E_2')$, $$ (g_1, E_1) \preceq_{\text{rep}} (g_2, E_2) \iff (g_1', E_1') \preceq_{\text{rep}} (g_2', E_2'). $$

Proof (left descent). Take $m \in G'$ with $m \cdot E_1 = E_1'$ and $\alpha := g_1^{-1} g_1' m \in P_{E_1}$. Assume $(g_1, E_1) \preceq_{\text{rep}} (g_2, E_2)$ with witness $n$. Take $n'' := n m^{-1}$:

  • Face-chain: $n'' \cdot E_1' = n m^{-1} \cdot (m \cdot E_1) = n \cdot E_1 \preceq E_2$.
  • Membership: $(g_1')^{-1} g_2 n'' = m \alpha^{-1} g_1^{-1} g_2 n m^{-1}$; substitute $g_1^{-1} g_2 n \in P_{E_1}$ and use (P1) with $m$ to conclude $m \alpha^{-1} (g_1^{-1} g_2 n) m^{-1} \in m P_{E_1} m^{-1} = P_{m \cdot E_1} = P_{E_1'}$.

Reverse direction: symmetric via $m^{-1}$.

Proof (right descent). Take $m \in G'$ with $m \cdot E_2 = E_2'$ and $\beta := g_2^{-1} g_2' m \in P_{E_2}$. Assume $(g_1, E_1) \preceq_{\text{rep}} (g_2, E_2)$ with witness $n$. Take $n'' := m n$:

  • Face-chain: $n'' \cdot E_1 = m \cdot (n \cdot E_1) \preceq m \cdot E_2 = E_2'$.
  • Membership: $\beta \in P_{E_2}$, and by (P0) with $n \cdot E_1 \preceq E_2$: $\beta \in P_{n \cdot E_1}$. By (P1): $\beta = n p n^{-1}$ for some $p \in P_{E_1}$. Compute $g_1^{-1} g_2' n'' = (g_1^{-1} g_2 n) \cdot p \in P_{E_1} \cdot P_{E_1} = P_{E_1}$.

$\square$

Antisymmetry and partial-order structure

Theorem 3 (antisymmetry mod $\sim$). If $(g_1, E_1) \preceq_{\text{rep}} (g_2, E_2)$ and $(g_2, E_2) \preceq_{\text{rep}} (g_1, E_1)$, then $(g_1, E_1) \sim (g_2, E_2)$.

Proof. From witnesses $n_1$ and $n_2$ respectively, we get $(n_2 n_1) \cdot E_1 \preceq E_1$. The $G$-action is cellular (Cellular G-action on an abstract cell complex), hence dimension preserving: $\dim((n_2 n_1) \cdot E_1) = \dim E_1$. Strict monotonicity of $\dim$ along a proper face-chain (Abstract cell complex) forces $(n_2 n_1) \cdot E_1 = E_1$, so $n_1 \cdot E_1 = E_2$, and the $P_{E_1}$-membership from the $n_1$-witness is exactly the $\sim$-witness. $\square$

Assembling Theorems 1–3 with the descent proposition:

Corollary. $\preceq$ is a partial order on $X$, and the definition coincides with the descended single-witness form $\preceq_{\text{rep}}$.

Which axioms enter which theorem

Theorem Axioms used
Definition + reflexivity none (reflexivity of $X'$'s $\preceq$)
Theorem 1 (definition ⇔ single-witness) none beyond the definition of $\sim$
Theorem 2 (transitivity) (P0), (P1)
Descent proposition (P0), (P1)
Theorem 3 (antisymmetry mod $\sim$) dim preservation (cellular action) + strict monotonicity of $\dim$

Note: (P2) does not enter this node. It is the axiom needed for injectivity of $\iota$, i.e.\ for $\iota$ to be order-reflecting (ι : X' → G ×^P X' is a cellular embedding (poset form) clause (1)), not for the face relation itself.

Consequences

  • The embedding $\iota : X' \to X$, $E \mapsto [(1, E)]$, is order-preserving: for $F \preceq E$ in $X'$, the definition with $g := 1$ gives $\iota F \preceq \iota E$ immediately.
  • Order-reflection of $\iota$ requires (P2); see ι : X' → G ×^P X' is a cellular embedding (poset form) clause (2).
  • The dimension function $\dim([(g, E)]) := \dim E$ is well-defined because $\sim$ forces $E_2 = n \cdot E_1$ for some $n \in G'$, and the $G$-action is dimension-preserving.
  • Together with local finiteness of $X'$ (inherited via $G$-translates), this equips $X$ with the abstract-cell-complex and $G$-cell-complex instances used by CW structure and QFD property on G ×^P X'.

Lean formalization

Bridge between the math body and the Lean definition

The math body's definition (symmetric same-$g$ form) and the Lean library's InductionLe (Theorem 1's single-witness form) are two presentations of the same relation on $G \times X'$:

  • Body: $[(g_1, E_1)] \preceq [(g_2, E_2)] \iff \exists\, g,\; F \preceq E$ in $X'$ with same-$g$ representatives.
  • Lean: InductionLe d (g₁, E₁) (g₂, E₂) $\iff \exists\, n \in G',\; n \cdot E_1 \preceq E_2 \wedge g_1^{-1} g_2 n \in P_{E_1}$.

Theorem 1 is the equivalence. Lean takes the single-witness form as the operational definition — it makes each well-definedness lemma provable by direct group calculation and avoids threading existentially-quantified representatives through the descent proof. The name mirrors InductionRel (the pre-quotient equivalence relation from [[node:equivariant_sheaves.induction_GxP_X]]): same syntactic shape, "$=$" replaced by "$\preceq$".

Face relation and the five well-definedness lemmas

def InductionLe (g₁E₁ g₂E₂ : G × X') : Prop :=
  ∃ n ∈ d.G', n • g₁E₁.2 ≤ g₂E₂.2 ∧
              g₁E₁.1⁻¹ * g₂E₂.1 * n ∈ d.P g₁E₁.2

Each theorem of the math body has a dedicated Lean lemma:

Theorem (body) Lean lemma Axioms used
Reflexivity of $\preceq$ InductionLe_refl $1 \in G'$, $1 \in P_E$
Theorem 2 (transitivity) InductionLe_trans (P0), (P1)
Descent (left) InductionLe_left_descends (P1)
Descent (right) InductionLe_right_descends (P0), (P1)
Theorem 3 (antisymmetry mod $\sim$) InductionLe_antisymm GCellComplex.smul_dim + AbstractCellComplex.dim_lt

The Theorem 1 (⇒) calculation — combining two $\sim$-witnesses into a single InductionLe-witness via $n := n_2^{-1} n_1$ and the $p_1 \cdot n_1^{-1}(n_2 p_2^{-1} n_2^{-1}) n_1$ residual identity — is not a standalone Lean lemma. It is instead the same computation that appears inside InductionLe_trans and InductionLe_*_descends: those lemmas each take two witnesses (a $\sim$ one and an InductionLe one) and produce a single InductionLe witness by the same (P0)+(P1) conjugation trick.

PartialOrder instance

instance : PartialOrder (InducedSpace d) where
  le := Quotient.lift₂ (InductionLe d) <descent proof>
  le_refl q     := Quotient.inductionOn q (InductionLe_refl d)
  le_trans      := Quotient.inductionOn₃ _ _ _ (fun _ _ _ => InductionLe_trans d)
  le_antisymm   := Quotient.inductionOn₂ _ _
    (fun _ _ h₁ h₂ => Quotient.sound (InductionLe_antisymm d h₁ h₂))

The Quotient.lift₂ side condition (that InductionLe respects $\sim$ on both arguments) is discharged by InductionLe_left_descends + InductionLe_right_descends. Reflexivity, transitivity, antisymmetry lift through Quotient.inductionOn{,₂,₃} from their representative-level counterparts.

Dimension and cell-complex instances (the Consequences bullets)

InducedSpace.dim realises $\dim([(g, E)]) := \dim E$ via Quotient.lift; well-definedness comes from GCellComplex.smul_dim (the $G$-action on $X'$ is dimension-preserving), and the compatibility rewrites are dim_iota, dim_smul.

def dim : InducedSpace d → ℕ :=
  Quotient.lift (fun gE : G × X' => AbstractCellComplex.dim gE.2) ...

The AbstractCellComplex (InducedSpace d) instance packages dim with:

  • dim_lt proved by case-splitting on the InductionLe witness: either $n E_1 = E_2$ (giving $\sim$, hence class equality, hence contradiction) or $n E_1 < E_2$ (giving strict dim by AbstractCellComplex.dim_lt on $X'$). This mirrors Theorem 3.
  • exists_face_dim_pred lifts the corresponding axiom on $X'$ through the same-$g$ generator (take $E' \prec E$ with $\dim E' + 1 = \dim E$; then $[(g, E')] \prec [(g, E)]$).

Finally GCellComplex G (InducedSpace d) is the cellular-action compatibility: smul_le is invariance of InductionLe under simultaneous left translation (same $n$ witness works), smul_dim is dim_smul.

Together with IsLocallyFinite (inherited via $G$-translates), this gives the full poset-level cell-complex structure on the induced space that CW structure and QFD property on G ×^P X' uses.

Follow-ups

A Relation.ReflTransGen-based reformulation of InductionLe (using the same-$g$ generator $g \cdot \iota F \preceq g \cdot \iota E$ for $F \preceq E$) plus an explicit equivalence lemma Relation.ReflTransGen ... ↔ InductionLe would let a reader match the body's Definition to a Lean object directly. Everything needed for the proof is already in place (transitivity plus descent), so this is a well-scoped follow-up.
